correctness.rationale: A degree-five map is a basepoint-free pencil <F,G> of binary quintics. Over F2 all three rational target fibres are F,G,F+G; unramifiedness at each target rational point is equivalent to all three homogeneous quintics squarefree. The exact affine gcd/derivative plus infinity condition exhaustively enumerates all 63 nonzero masks and 24 squarefree forms; independent SymPy polynomial arithmetic reconstructed 22 admissible pencils and all six source PGL2(F2) transformations, yielding the five listed disjoint orbits and 132 ordered map bases. The Wronskian in characteristic 2 is the square of the quartic AD+BC, and actual residue-field Hasse coefficient order, not ordinary derivative multiplicity, distinguishes ramification indices 2 and 5. Independent critical-polynomial and branch-resultant calculations reproduce all five branch degrees and the quadratic branch collision. This proves the finite classification, not a general-q or general-degree result.

value.rationale: Avoiding ramification at all three rational target points is a canonical small-field Hurwitz-locus condition, relevant for constructing finite-field covers and their fibre products. The exact orbit list distinguishes arithmetically and geometrically inequivalent covers, including wild-versus-tame and a nontrivial collision of four wild critical points over two branch values; these facts are not read off a total map count. F2 and degree five are justified by the smallest field with three rational targets and the first coexistence of these ramification patterns.

final_claim: There are exactly 132 degree-five F2-rational morphisms P1→P1 with both coordinate systems fixed that are unramified over all three rational target points, 22 unlabelled target pencils and precisely five source-target orbit classes of sizes 3,1,6,6,6 with classified source/branch Frobenius degrees and tame/wild ramification.
